classification.difficultyReason: Compare three distances and recognise two equally close points.

content.prompt: Which of the points $A$, $B$, or $C$ are closest to the point $(2,3)$?

spec.description: Both axes have arrows at both ends and integer ticks at −3, −2, −1, 1, 2 and 3. Red dashed connections join the reference point to each candidate. No grid. The origin letter is omitted under the house graph convention.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied coordinates and connections are visible; the closest points are not identified.

answer.short: $B$ and $C$ are both $5$ units from $(2,3)$. Compare the distances using the distance formula.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}PA&=\sqrt{(3-2)^2+(-2-3)^2}\\PA&=\sqrt{26}\\PB&=\sqrt{(-1-2)^2+(-1-3)^2}\\PB&=5\\PC&=\sqrt{(-3-2)^2+(3-3)^2}\\PC&=5\end{aligned}$$
Since $5<\sqrt{26}$, $B$ and $C$ are equally closest, each $5$ units away.
